quarterly_data.signal: CEO Morten Wierod: Q3 2026 orders were just above $12 billion, a comparable increase of 40%, with data centers the standout at triple-digit growth 'with no signs of demand softening or CapEx hesitation'; comparable revenue grew 14% (net pricing just about 2%), operational EBITA rose 24% to $2 billion and the 20.8% operational EBITA margin is ABB's strongest Q3 margin ever (EBIT margin 19%, return on capital employed 29.9%). Comparable orders rose 70% in the Americas (U.S. up 82%, base orders about 50%), 10% in Europe and 29% in Asia, Middle East and Africa (China up 25%). EPS of $0.65 fell 2%, mainly on a non-cash unrealized FX hedge linked to the Rotork acquisition (about $115 million) and lower results in discontinued operations.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 orders just above $12 billion (+40% comparable); operational EBITA margin 20.8%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Christian Nilsson: Electrification orders reached a record of close to $7.7 billion, up 70%, with data centers at triple-digit growth and orders excluding data centers up at a high-teens rate (utility grid refurbishment and expansion, commercial buildings); Electrification revenue was $5.4 billion (+21% comparable, pricing around 3%, now broadly offsetting commodity inflation) and operational EBITA $1.4 billion at a record 25.6% margin. Motion orders were $2.5 billion (+12%, grid investments, HVAC and data-center cooling), revenue $2.3 billion (+9%) and margin 19.1% (down 100 basis points, about 40 from Gamesa Electric); Automation orders were stable at $2.1 billion, revenue $2.1 billion (+5%) and margin 14.8%. CEO: the data-center business is by far mainly with hyperscalers and colocators, with some neocloud.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrification orders close to $7.7 billion (+70%); margin 25.6%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Morten Wierod: book-to-bill reached 1.24 and the order backlog expanded to just about $32 billion, almost equal to 2025 revenues, skewed toward longer delivery times by data center, marine and rail orders; CFO Christian Nilsson: about 40% of it converts next year. Data-center lead times run from 12 to 24 months, so orders booked this year ship in 2027 or 2028; most large orders carry significant advance payments or clear cancellation policies for permitted, grid-connected and funded sites, and ABB sees no pre-ordering.
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog just about $32 billion; book-to-bill 1.24

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Morten Wierod: for Q4 ABB expects comparable revenue growth broadly similar to Q3 and a slightly smaller-than-usual seasonal margin decline (excluding a real estate sale gain of about 240 million Swiss francs in Q4); for full-year 2026 it now expects comparable growth in the low teens range and a reported operational EBITA margin improvement of at least 270 basis points from 2025, including real estate sales. CFO Christian Nilsson: Electrification Q4 comparable growth in the high teens to low 20% range, Motion similar to Q3 with a slight sequential margin improvement, Automation low to mid-single digits with a broadly stable margin; year-to-date free cash flow of $3.7 billion and a path to about $5 billion for the year; capex around $1 billion this year and not expected to grow significantly over the next few years.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 comparable growth low teens; operational EBITA margin up at least 270 basis points

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Morten Wierod: after 12 to 18 months of very strong demand some product lines, mostly in Electrification, are approaching high utilization until ongoing capacity investments become fully operational during 2027; capex is tracking at around $1 billion, much of it for Electrification factories, and ABB is 'very seldom' the bottleneck for data-center projects, where power transformers and gas turbines are longer-lead items.

CEO Morten Wierod: ABB launched its Infinitus direct-current portfolio for AI data centers across DC architectures from source to rack, built on five modular building blocks, with solid-state transformers available to order in the second half of 2027; he says DC enables rack densities up to one megawatt and facilities from 200 megawatts to 1.5 gigawatts, a 500-megawatt data center moving to DC can cut conversion losses by more than 5%, and in a target DC architecture as much as 75% of electrical power infrastructure spend can sit in the gray space (about 55% in legacy AC), expanding ABB's addressable scope; he views the sidecar as an interim solution and sees ABB as a disruptor in 800 V DC.
quarterly_data.figure: solid-state transformers available to order in H2 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Morten Wierod: ABB will take a 51% controlling stake in a joint venture formed with Mitsubishi Electric's low-voltage power distribution business (circuit breakers, motor starters, contactors, control devices, energy measurement), with a firm midterm path to full ownership; the business has around 2,800 employees and around $640 million of fiscal 2025 revenue, mostly in Japan, at a low double-digit EBITA margin, ABB targets at least a 20% operational EBITA margin five years after completion, and closing is expected in the second half of 2027. The Rotork acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, and ABB aims to complete the robotics divestment by the end of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: JV business revenue around $640 million (fiscal 2025); about 2,800 employees
